title: Pair Patterns
kicker: ROLES · THE MIDDLE · LOB TARGETS · SWITCHES · AUSTRALIAN FORMATION · PRE-POINT PLANS
opener_line: A pair wins with shared patterns: one player builds, the other finishes, both move together.
intro: Plenty of club pairs are really two individuals who happen to share a court. Each of them hits good shots, yet nobody has settled who builds the point, who finishes it, who owns the ball through the middle or what happens when a lob sails over one of them. The ten drills in this chapter turn those open questions into shared answers, so your partner’s next move stops being a surprise and starts being something you can lean on.

The order runs from simple roles to full plans. The first drills give each side of the court a job: the drive player builds, the revés player finishes. The middle of the chapter covers the moments pairs most often lose together, such as middle balls, switches and the gap after a line ball. The last drills add a serving formation and a plan you agree between points. Use your regular partner where you can, and talk each drill through before the first ball.

pillars.title: Clear roles
pillars.text: The right side builds with patience, the left side finishes. Both of you know the job before the ball is struck.

pillars.title: One middle rule
pillars.text: Agree who owns the centre ball and its exceptions, then apply that rule the same way every time.

pillars.title: Move together
pillars.text: Same depth, same time. When one of you goes back or comes forward, the other goes too.

pillars.title: Plan, then play
pillars.text: Agree a short pattern between points and carry it out, even when the score gets tight.

box.label: PAIR PRINCIPLE
box.text: If you and your partner would answer ‘whose ball is that?’ differently, the opponents already have a target. Settle the answer in training, not in the middle of a rally.

drills.title: Set up the revés finisher.
drills.summary: A builds with deep volleys until the defenders send a short lob to the left half, where B finishes it. B’s overhead winners count double.
drills.setup: Your pair holds the net, A on the right and B on the left. C and D defend from the back glass. C opens every point with a lob towards A.
run: Play the point out. A builds: volleys deep into the corners and through the middle, never short and never forced.
B finishes. When a lob on the left half is short enough to attack, B plays the víbora into the corner or the x3; otherwise a deep bandeja.
Scoring: a point won by B’s overhead counts 2, any other point your pair wins counts 1, and every point C and D win counts 1.
Play to 11. Then C and D take the net and run the same pattern.
drills.decision: A reads which volley buys the short lob: depth into the back glass, or a ball at the weaker lobber’s feet. B reads which lob is really there to attack.
drills.watch: A tries to win the point alone from a building ball. Fix: A only goes for a winner from a high, easy ball inside the service box.
drills.up: C and D may lob anywhere, so B must also cover the middle lob with an overhead on the forehand side.
drills.down: C and D play only cross-court lobs to the left half, at medium height.
drills.pass: Your pair reaches 11 first, with at least four points finished by B’s overhead.
drills.caption: A volleys deep into D’s corner. D’s lob lands short on the left, and B steps back to finish.

drills.title: Drive builder: patience on the right.
drills.summary: From the back of the right side, A must play four neutral balls before attacking is allowed, building calmly against a net pair.
drills.setup: Your pair starts behind the service line, A on the right. The opponents hold the net. B may only lob; A may play anything but counts each shot aloud.
run: C starts each point with a deep volley to A. Play it out, with A keeping count of every shot.
Up to and including four, A may only play neutral balls: low at a net player’s feet, a deep lob, or a slow ball through the middle.
From the fifth shot, A may attack: a firm drive at the body, a passing ball, or a chiquita and move up. An earlier attack loses the point.
Play to 11, then swap: B builds from the left with the same count and A may only lob.
drills.decision: Which neutral ball fits: low when the net player hangs back, a lob when that player crowds the net, the middle when both drift wide.
drills.watch: Neutral balls hit too hard, so the pace comes straight back at your feet. Fix: play at about two-thirds pace and let depth do the work.
drills.up: Raise the count to seven shots, or allow C and D to smash.
drills.down: Lower the count to three, and C and D volley at medium pace.
drills.pass: A makes no more than two errors before the fifth shot in a game to 11.
drills.caption: A’s two most useful neutral balls from the right: low at C’s feet, or a lob over C into the deep corner.

drills.title: Own the middle: the forehand rule.
drills.summary: F sends balls through the middle and the pair applies one agreed rule (B’s forehand takes it) plus two exceptions, with a call every time.
drills.setup: Both partners right-handed, about 2.5 m from the net. F with a basket at the far back glass, shifting position between feeds. With a left-hander in the pair, agree your own rule first.
run: Say the rule aloud first: for two right-handers, B on the left has the forehand towards the centre, so middle volleys and lobs belong to B.
Exception one: if A is clearly closer to the net, A takes the middle volley. Exception two: if B has just been pulled wide, A takes it.
F feeds 20 middle balls in a random mix of volleys, low balls and lobs. Whoever plays it calls ‘mine’; the partner answers ‘yours’.
Second set: F feeds in pairs, the first ball wide to pull B out, the second through the middle.
drills.decision: On the first step: standard case, so B’s forehand, or does an exception apply? You should both reach the same answer, not follow whoever shouts first.
drills.watch: Both players reaching, or neither moving. Fix: B moves first on every middle ball; A goes only when B’s first step shows the ball is out of reach.
drills.up: F feeds faster, with a two-second gap, and mixes in balls slightly off the centre.
drills.down: Only waist-high middle volleys, no lobs, and a four-second gap.
drills.pass: 17 of 20 middle balls played by the right player, with a clear call.
drills.caption: A ball through the middle: B moves first, because for two right-handers B’s forehand faces the centre.

drills.title: Lob the backhand shoulder, then close.
drills.summary: From the back, your pair lobs over a net player’s backhand shoulder into a deep zone, then both move up once the lob is past that player.
drills.setup: Your pair defends from the back; the opponents start at the net. Mark T1 behind C: the last three metres before the glass, on the centre side of C’s half.
run: C starts with a low ball. Rally until one of you has a ball you can lob with control, then aim for T1.
If the lob clears C into T1, A and B move forward together and take the net side by side.
Points your pair wins after a T1 lob and a shared close count 2; all other points count 1.
Play to 11. Then move T1 behind D, this time on the side-wall side, since a right-hander on the left has the backhand by the side wall.
drills.decision: Before the point: which shoulder? On the right a right-hander’s backhand faces the centre, on the left it is by the wall; left-handers are reversed. During it: can you lob from this ball, and is the lob truly past?
drills.watch: Moving up behind a lob the net player can still reach. Fix: go forward only when the net player turns to chase it, never on your own contact.
drills.up: C and D may smash any lob that lands short of T1.
drills.down: T1 covers the whole back half of C’s side, and C and D volley at medium pace.
drills.pass: At least five lobs into T1 in a game to 11, and a shared close after each.
drills.caption: A lobs over C’s backhand shoulder into T1. As C turns to chase, A and B move up to the net together.

drills.title: The Australian serve pattern.
drills.summary: B starts at the net directly in front of the server, A serves and crosses to the other half, and the pair attacks the forced line return.
drills.setup: A serves from the right, one foot behind the service line. B takes the net on A’s half, a little towards the side wall so the serve misses B. C receives.
run: Nothing in the rules ties the server’s partner to one spot on their own side, so this is legal. A serve that hits B is a fault, so B checks the spot every point.
A serves towards the centre line to take away the wide angle, then moves diagonally forward to the left half. C’s cross-court return now meets B.
A takes the return down the line and plays it deep cross-court or lobs. Afterwards the pair returns to its usual sides.
A serves ten points, alternating boxes as in a game: from the left box, B stands on the left and A crosses right. Then B serves ten.
drills.decision: Is the formation worth it against this receiver? Against habitual cross-court returners, yes. A decides how early to cross without leaving the right half open.
drills.watch: A crosses too late and the line return passes A. Fix: A’s first step after the serve goes diagonally forward to the left.
drills.up: Play a full set, with B choosing the formation by signal on no more than half your serves.
drills.down: C returns at medium pace, cross-court or down the line only, no lobs.
drills.pass: Win at least six of A’s ten serving points.
drills.caption: B blocks the cross-court return, so C goes down the line, where A has crossed to cover after serving.

drills.title: Mine, switch or glass.
drills.summary: F lobs over B at varied heights and depths. B makes one of three calls, and the pair must be level on its new sides for ball two.
drills.setup: Your pair starts in net position, about 2.5 m from the net. F with a basket at the far back glass, on the half diagonal to B, ready to lob.
run: F lobs cross-court over B, changing height and depth each time. B calls before the ball peaks: ‘mine’, ‘switch’ or ‘glass’.
‘Mine’: B backs up and plays a deep bandeja. ‘Switch’: A crosses behind B and plays it, B takes the right half. ‘Glass’: both drop back, B plays it off the glass.
Whatever the call, F feeds a second ball at once, low to whoever is now on the right. The pair must be level on its new halves.
Ten sequences per set. Then F moves to the other diagonal and lobs over A, so A makes the calls.
drills.decision: B judges in one look whether an overhead going back is possible or whether the lob is too deep. A crosses only on ‘switch’, never on a guess.
drills.watch: A late call, so both chase or both stop. Fix: B calls while the ball is still rising, and A reacts to the word, not the flight.
drills.up: Some lobs go over the middle, where either player may own them.
drills.down: Only two calls, ‘mine’ or ‘switch’, and lobs of medium height.
drills.pass: 8 of 10 sequences with the right call before the peak and the pair level for ball two.
drills.caption: A deep lob over B: B calls ‘switch’, A crosses behind B to play it, and B takes the right half.

drills.title: Shut the middle after the line.
drills.summary: When one of you volleys down the line, the partner slides in to close the middle, leaving only a tight angle or a lob.
drills.setup: Your pair volleys from net position; the opponents play from the back. Place a cone on the centre line, level with you, as the slider’s reference.
run: C starts with a medium ball to A. A volleys down the line, deep to D. Every rally in this set starts this way.
As A’s volley crosses the net, A holds the line and B slides until about a racket’s length from the cone.
D plays any shot and the point is live. A winning volley by B off a middle ball scores 2; other points count 1.
Play to 11. Then C starts to B, B volleys down the line to C, and A closes the middle.
drills.decision: Read where your partner’s ball went. Line ball: the partner closes the middle. Cross-court ball: both stay central. Read it on your partner’s contact.
drills.watch: B watches the opponent in front and stays wide, leaving a gap. Fix: B tracks the ball, not the player, and steps in as A’s volley crosses.
drills.up: C and D may also lob over the player who slid, so the pair must handle a switch.
drills.down: D replies only through the middle or down the line, at medium pace.
drills.pass: No ball passes between you through the middle in a game to 11.
drills.caption: A volleys down the line to D. B slides towards the cone, so D’s middle reply runs into B’s racket.

drills.title: Pick a target.
drills.summary: Your pair sends every ball to one chosen opponent, with one free ball per point to the other player that scores double if it wins.
drills.setup: Normal 2 v 2 from a serve. Before each game, A and B quietly choose the target. Cones along the far side’s extended centre line mark the halves.
run: Your pair plays every ball into the target’s half. A ball into the other half that is not your free ball loses the point.
Each point you have one free ball into the other half. Save it for when the target’s partner drifts across to help.
Scoring: a point won with the free ball counts 2, a point lost by a target error counts 2 for you, and every other point counts 1.
C and D play normally. Play four games, changing the target after any game if you want.
drills.decision: How to keep pressure on one player without giving that player a rhythm, and when the free ball is worth spending: only when the target’s partner is out of position.
drills.watch: Feeding the target the same ball until it is grooved. Fix: change height, pace and depth on every shot, never three alike in a row.
drills.up: No free ball: every shot of every point goes to the target.
drills.down: Two free balls per point, and C and D may not smash.
drills.pass: Win at least three of the four games, with six or more points from target errors.
drills.caption: C is the target: A plays low at C’s feet, B lobs into C’s corner. Every ball goes to C’s half.

drills.title: The pre-point plan.
drills.summary: Before every point, each pair agrees a short plan within the 20 seconds allowed, and scores for carrying it out as well as for winning.
drills.setup: Normal 2 v 2. Serving plans: ‘Glass’ (serve into the side glass, first volley deep middle) and ‘Body’ (serve at the receiver, first volley into the receiver’s corner). Receiving: ‘Over’ (lob the net player, close) and ‘Low’.
run: Between points, the serving pair names a serving plan and the receivers a receiving plan, quietly. ‘Low’ means the return goes at the server’s feet.
Each plan has three parts: first shot, second shot and who covers the middle lob. Confirm all three every time.
Play the point. Afterwards each pair says honestly whether it carried out its first two shots.
Scoring: won with the plan 3, won without it 1, lost with the plan 1, lost without it 0. Play six games and compare totals.
drills.decision: Which plan fits this score, this server and the opponents’ last point. Then the harder part: sticking to it once the ball is moving.
drills.watch: Plans that grow every point and run past 20 seconds. Fix: one word names the plan and the partner repeats it back.
drills.up: Add an Australian formation plan, and score plans only from 30–30 or deuce.
drills.down: Only the serving pair plans; the receiving pair plays freely.
drills.pass: Carry out the plan on at least two in every three points over six games.
drills.caption: Plan ‘Body’: A serves at C and moves in to play the first volley deep into C’s corner.

drills.title: Same depth, same time.
drills.summary: F feeds mixed sequences and calls ‘freeze’ after each of your shots. You score only if you are level and both shifted towards the ball.
drills.setup: Your pair starts in net position. F feeds from a basket on the far side, from different spots. A spare player by the side glass can judge.
run: F feeds sequences of six balls: volleys, a deep lob that pushes you back, a short ball that brings you forward and some wide balls.
After each of your shots, F calls ‘freeze’. Both of you stop exactly where you are, without adjusting.
F checks two things: are you level, neither more than a metre ahead, and have you both shifted towards the ball’s side? Two yeses score 1.
Six sequences per round, then swap so F feeds more balls to the other player, who must now lead the movement.
drills.decision: Every move your partner makes is a move for you: back when your partner goes back, up when they come up, across when the ball goes wide.
drills.watch: One player stays at the net while the other is lobbed back, opening a diagonal gap. Fix: when your partner turns to chase a lob, drop back alongside.
drills.up: F calls ‘freeze’ only at random, two or three times per sequence, so you can’t prepare for it.
drills.down: Four-ball sequences at a slow pace with a three-second gap.
drills.pass: At least 30 of 36 freezes with both checks passed.
drills.caption: F lobs over A. A goes back to play it, and B drops back too so the pair stays level.
